about.title: Kingsburg Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription:
When a death on Mountain View Avenue or Sierra Street takes a parent, spouse or child, the paperwork that follows can feel impossible. Kingsburg is a small town of about 11,800 people in Fresno County, and in 2025 public records list 20 injury collisions, 30 people hurt and 2 traffic deaths.

A California wrongful death claim is a civil action. It runs separately from any criminal case, and it exists so surviving relatives can recover funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the harder-to-measure loss of love, companionship and guidance. Standing is limited: a spouse or registered domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. The filing window is two years from the date of death, and it shrinks considerably when a public agency is involved.

We handle California wrongful death claims on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

about.ctaText: Talk with us about your family's options

items.title: We sort out who can file
items.desc: California limits who may bring a wrongful death claim, starting with a spouse or domestic partner and children, then certain dependents and heirs. We can explain where your family fits before anything is filed.

items.title: We keep the two-year clock in view
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the deadline is far shorter if a city, county or state agency may share responsibility. Reaching out early protects your ability to act.

items.title: We separate the civil claim from the criminal case
items.desc: A wrongful death action is a civil matter and moves forward whether or not prosecutors ever file charges. It seeks funeral costs, lost financial support, and compensation for the loss of love, companionship and guidance.

items.question: My family member died in a crash on Mountain View Avenue in Kingsburg. Does it matter that no one was charged?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and does not depend on a criminal case being opened or won. We review the collision report, witness accounts and insurance coverage directly. Kingsburg's collision records are public, and we can request them for you.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: The surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the children have the first right to file. If there are none, certain financially dependent relatives and other heirs may qualify. Because the rules are specific, it helps to have an attorney confirm standing before the claim is prepared.

items.question: How long do we have, and what does this cost?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death, but if a government entity is involved the deadline can be a matter of months. We handle these claims on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless we recover.
